text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
HELSINGIN SANOMAT
- Loans from pension funds (TEL) to become clearly cheaper for companies if plans to lower the regulated interest rate to four percent from 5.5 percent are accepted in talks today.
- Economic growth does not bring jobs to the over 45-year-old unemployed, statistics show.
- Parliament officials not prepared to revise plans to build a new parliament building with offices for MPs assistants despite criticism that existing buildings are available.
- Social democrats want to make it possible for the state to force mergers between municipalities. Centre Party opposed.
- The group of professors appointed by the government to examine pros and cons of EMU membership will publish its report on May 6 but the government will be briefed on it on April 23.
- 101 MPs in the 200-seat legislature would allow selling wines in retail outlets, they say in a written question to the government.
KAUPPALEHTI

- Competition between teleoperators about corporate clients is getting tougher. Telivo has made an agreement with state-owned Hansel, which will give it a foothold on the public and coporate sector market.
- There are signs in the Nordic countries that banks may try to offset smaller lending margins with looser credit criteria to boost volume, warns Danish Den Danske Bank's CEO Knud Sorensen.

- Finnish employers will embrace their European counterparts' attitudes in a few years, says Tuulikki Kannisto, secretary of international affairs at the Central Organisation of Finnish Trade Unions (SAK).
AAMULEHTI
- Finnish firms are issuing bonds with warrants to their managaments at near record pace this year.
- Long forgotten hotel construction plans are moving again but the recovering booking situation is not strong enough and there are signs of overheating, industry official says.
- Universities are competing more than before for talented students; some offer free lodging, personal computers and free bus travel.
TURUN SANOMAT
- Bids for Turku telephone operator Turun Puhelin which the City of Turku is selling are in the region of 500 million markka, sources say.

- Finland's markka denominated debt will rise until next decade but the finance ministry's target is that the debt-to-GDP ratio would start falling and reach 65 percent by 2001 from 70.8 percent this year, ministry deputy director Seppo Suokko says.
